natural_body: Price-sensitive SMBs: 40% off drove signup +31%, revenue +18%, retention -12%.

first.rationale:
Both declining metrics (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) point at the funnel, and the objective is sustainable long-term qualified revenue, so I am steering away from the competitor-response reflex. memory_73 is the clearest disqualifier: 40% off bought signups (+31%) and short-run revenue (+18%) but cost retention (-12%), which is exactly the trade that looks good this quarter and bad on a long horizon. Referral incentives (memory_57) are healthy but act on established customers and do nothing for the two metrics actually degrading. Enterprise sales-assist (memory_44) is real but is a different segment from where the bleeding is.

That leaves simplify_onboarding vs activation_messaging. I am picking onboarding because completion is upstream of activation, so a completion lift should partially propagate; but I am spending both verification pulls on memory_31 and memory_86 specifically because they are suspiciously convergent. Two separate consolidations (day 12, day 52) both claiming that trimming the signup/onboarding path lifted activation could be two independent replications — or one original experiment that got re-consolidated and now reads as corroboration it never earned. Inherited memory is generally reliable, but agreement between two summaries is worthless if they share a source, and I would rather find that out before committing the only slot this week than after. If the archive shows a single underlying record, my confidence in the effect size drops sharply and activation_messaging (memory_91, independent) becomes competitive.

Downstream value risk: cutting required signup fields is not value-neutral. memory_44 says enterprise pipeline quality depends on the demo-request/sales-assisted path, and that routing likely keys off exactly the fields a simplification would remove. An SMB activation win that quietly degrades enterprise lead qualification would show up as a clean success on the experiment dashboard and as a loss in qualified revenue two quarters out. So: standard experiment, segment-gated to self-serve SMB, enterprise routing fields left untouched, and retention plus downstream pipeline quality instrumented as guardrails rather than just measuring completion. Also worth noting all of these records predate the competitor's entry pricing, so prior effect sizes may not transfer cleanly to current conditions.
